scope: P4-TROPICAL-20 semantics; no runtime or public-contract change

canonical_hazard_type.meaning: confirmed tropical cyclone system; generic parent for depression, tropical storm and hurricane/typhoon-strength tropical cyclones

potential_tropical_cyclone.meaning: disturbance not yet a tropical cyclone but capable of producing tropical-storm or hurricane conditions and eligible for advisories

tropical_depression.meaning: confirmed tropical cyclone in depression stage

tropical_storm.meaning: confirmed tropical cyclone in tropical-storm stage

hurricane_strength_tropical_cyclone.meaning: confirmed tropical cyclone at hurricane/typhoon strength according to the responsible authority

subtropical_cyclone.meaning: subtropical cyclone; structurally distinct status that must remain source-reported

post_tropical_cyclone.meaning: former tropical cyclone no longer possessing sufficient tropical characteristics

regional_terminology.rule: regional naming is provenance/terminology, not by itself a different hazard family

intensity_semantics.rule: wind averaging period and responsible authority must be preserved before cross-provider comparison

forecast_products.design_question: retain as event metadata or define explicit resource semantics

storm_surge.relationship: possible associated hazard requiring its own source evidence

authoritative_references.finding: NHC classifies tropical depressions, tropical storms, hurricanes and major hurricanes by sustained wind thresholds.
Potential/pre-/post-tropical and tropical cyclone terms have distinct lifecycle meanings; post-tropical is no longer tropical.
Potential tropical cyclone advisories can be issued before a disturbance becomes a tropical cyclone; forecast status can become post-tropical.
Hurricane, typhoon and cyclone terminology varies by basin for the same broad tropical-cyclone phenomenon.
Tropical cyclone governance and naming are regional and involve multiple regional bodies.

invariants: Potential Tropical Cyclone is not a confirmed tropical cyclone.
Post-Tropical Cyclone is not a current tropical cyclone.
Tropical Depression, Tropical Storm and hurricane-strength stages remain distinguishable.
Hurricane, typhoon and cyclone are regional terminology, not automatically separate hazard families.
Track is not observed damage path.
Wind probability is not observed wind.
Tropical cyclone is not automatically storm surge.
GDACS is not a primary tropical-cyclone warning authority.
Aviation SIGMET is not a general public warning.
NHC coverage is not global coverage.
Provider ID is not a scoring axis.
Endpoint reachability is not coverage proof.
decisions_for_p4_tropical_30: Preserve source-reported lifecycle/classification additively instead of relying only on tropical_cyclone.
Represent potential and post-tropical states so they are not misreported as confirmed current tropical cyclones.
Preserve regional terminology separately from physical hazard family.
Keep alert stage independent from system classification and physical intensity.
Keep NHC track/cone/wind products distinct from observed event geometry.
Keep storm surge as a separate hazard requiring explicit source evidence.
Keep NHC, general weather warning, GDACS and aviation source roles distinct.
Design global coverage using provider-neutral regional authority semantics rather than provider ID priority.
